primitives.name: Control-Theme Traceability Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Purpose This table maps concrete runtime controls that ship in this repository to the generic *themes* used by widely-referenced AI governance frameworks, so an engineer (or a counterparty's engineer) can quickly see which control addresses which kind of concern.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{C}': 'set of runtime controls', '\\mathcal{F}': 'set of governance themes', '\\leq': 'partial order relation'}
primitives.assumptions: Each control \( c \in \mathcal{C} \) is associated with one or more themes \( f \in \mathcal{F} \).
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \( \mathcal{C} \) is empty or \( \mathcal{F} \) is undefined, \( \mathcal{T} \) becomes trivial.

layer2.mapping: The traceability kernel \( \mathcal{T} \) is isomorphic to a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes represent controls and themes, edges denote relevance.

layer2.mapping: The disclaimer operator \( \mathcal{D} \) filters out any \( \mathcal{L}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{C} \) from \( \mathcal{T} \), ensuring \( \mathcal{T} \subseteq \mathcal{R} \setminus (\mathcal{L} \cup \mathcal{A} \cup \mathcal{C}) \).

reasoning_traces.think:
The traceability kernel \( \mathcal{T} \) operates as a formal lattice \( (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \leq) \) where \( \mathcal{C} \) represents runtime controls and \( \mathcal{F} \) represents governance themes. The partial order \( \leq \) enables structured reasoning about relevance. The non-assertion disclaimer operator \( \mathcal{D} \) acts as a filter, excluding legal, audit, and certification claims from \( \mathcal{T} \), preserving its engineering-only scope. The snapshot stale matrix \( \mathcal{S} \) introduces a temporal dimension, flagging \( \mathcal{T} \) when \( \Delta \mathcal{T} > \tau_{\text{stale}} \), enforcing dynamic consistency. These primitives form a dual structure: \( \mathcal{T} \) provides forward traceability, while \( \mathcal{D} \) and \( \mathcal{S} \) provide backward constraints on validity and freshness. Failure modes include misalignment of \( \mathcal{C} \) with \( \mathcal{F} \), assertion leakage into \( \mathcal{T} \), and stale \( \mathcal{T} \) being treated as authoritative.
